title.en: Anomaly detection: statistical, proximity, density, clustering
title.zh: 异常检测：统计、邻近、密度、聚类

description.en: What counts as an anomaly and why it is hard to learn, then the four unsupervised families with every score computed by hand: z-score and Mahalanobis, k-th neighbour distance, relative density and a full LOF, and CBLOF.
description.zh: 什么算异常、为什么难学，然后是四类无监督方法，每个分数都手算：z 分数与马氏距离、第 k 邻居距离、相对密度与完整的 LOF、CBLOF。

name.en: Anomaly types, settings, why it is hard
name.zh: 异常的类型、设定、为什么难
统计检测：z 分数、马氏距离、Grubbs
基于密度的检测与 LOF

description.en: Thinking a standard supervised classifier solves anomaly detection
description.zh: 以为标准的监督分类器就能解决异常检测
在异常很稀有的数据上报告准确率

description.en: Using one distance threshold when densities differ
description.zh: 密度不同时仍用一个距离阈值

text.en: An **anomaly** (or outlier) is a data object that deviates so much from the normal objects that it looks as if a **different mechanism** generated it. A credit-card purchase in another country minutes after one at home; a sensor reading from a failing machine; a skin lesion among healthy ones.
text.zh: **异常**（anomaly，也叫离群点 outlier）是偏离正常对象很远、看上去像是由**另一种机制**产生的数据对象。比如在家刷卡几分钟后又在另一个国家刷了一笔；一台快坏的机器的传感器读数；一片健康皮肤上的一块病变。

items.en: **Uses:** banking and insurance fraud, bots and hacked accounts, intrusion and surveillance, sudden changes in customer behaviour, weather and seismic anomalies, melanoma checks, and cleaning outliers out of a data set before machine learning.
items.zh: **用途：**银行和保险欺诈、机器人账号和被盗账号、入侵和监控、客户行为突变、气象和地震异常、黑色素瘤筛查，以及在机器学习之前把离群点从数据里清掉。

items.en: **Not the same as noise.** Noise is random error in a measured value and should be removed *before* anomaly detection. An anomaly violates the mechanism that generates the normal data, and is often the interesting (even critical) part.
items.zh: **和噪声不是一回事。**噪声是测量值里的随机误差，应当在做异常检测*之前*去掉。异常违背的是产生正常数据的机制，往往正是有趣（甚至关键）的部分。

title.en: The ozone hole that was filtered out

body.en: In 1985 British Antarctic Survey data showed Antarctic ozone 10% below normal. NASA's Nimbus 7 satellite had recorded such values too, but the values were so low that a program treated them as noise and discarded them. Cleaning “noise” can delete the discovery.
body.zh: 1985 年英国南极调查的数据显示南极臭氧比正常低 10%。NASA 的 Nimbus 7 卫星其实也记录到了这样的值，但数值低得离谱，被程序当作噪声丢掉了。清洗“噪声”可能把发现一并删掉。

text.en: Three ways to pose the task
text.zh: 提出任务的三种方式

items.en: Find all $\mathbf{x} \in D$ whose **anomaly score** is above a threshold $t$ (the score function and $t$ learned from labelled normal data).
items.zh: 找出 $D$ 中**异常分数**超过阈值 $t$ 的所有 $\mathbf{x}$（分数函数和 $t$ 从带标签的正常数据学得）。

items.en: Find the **top-$n$** points by score $f(\mathbf{x})$: exploratory analysis, when you can only look at a few.
items.zh: 找出分数 $f(\mathbf{x})$ **最高的 $n$ 个**点：探索性分析，只能看有限几个时用。

items.en: Given mostly normal unlabelled data $D$ and a **new point** $\mathbf{x}$, score $\mathbf{x}$ against $D$: points arriving one by one (a stream).
items.zh: 给定大部分正常的无标签数据 $D$ 和一个**新点** $\mathbf{x}$，对照 $D$ 给 $\mathbf{x}$ 打分：数据逐条到来（数据流）。

chapter.en: What anomalies are and why they are hard

rows.en: the rest of the whole data set
rows.zh: 整个数据集的其余部分
网络流量里的一次入侵

rows.en: 10 °C: normal in a Paris winter, odd in a Paris summer; and in Melbourne, 10 °C in a day is ordinary any time of year
rows.zh: 10 °C：在巴黎冬天正常，夏天反常；而在墨尔本，一天里出现 10 °C 并不稀奇
一个有意义的上下文定义

rows.en: the data set, as a *group*; members may each look normal
rows.zh: 数据集，作为一个*群体*；成员单看可能都正常

rows.en: login attempts from many IPs in a short time; an odd subsequence in a time series
rows.zh: 短时间内来自许多 IP 的登录尝试；时间序列里一段奇怪的子序列

rows.en: relations among instances: sequence, space or graph
rows.zh: 实例之间的关系：序列、空间或图

text.en: **Contextual anomalies.** The attributes split into **contextual attributes** (they define the context: time, location) and **behavioural attributes** (what is judged: temperature). An object is a contextual anomaly if its behavioural attributes are unusual *given* its contextual ones. This generalises *local* anomalies, whose density deviates from its local area, because a context need not be spatial. The hard part is defining a meaningful context.
text.zh: **上下文异常。**属性分成**上下文属性**（定义上下文：时间、地点）和**行为属性**（被评判的：温度）。如果行为属性在*给定*上下文属性时不寻常，这个对象就是上下文异常。它推广了*局部*异常（密度和其局部区域差很多），因为上下文不一定是空间上的。难点是怎样定义有意义的上下文。

text.en: **Collective anomalies.** Each member of the group may be unremarkable; the *group* is not. Detecting them needs the relationships between instances (sequential, spatial or graph data), not only each instance's own values.
text.zh: **集体异常。**群体里的每个成员单看也许平平无奇，*群体*却不平常。检测它们需要实例之间的关系（序列、空间或图数据），不能只看每个实例自己的取值。

prompt.en: A heart rate of 120 beats/min is recorded for a patient who is asleep. Which type?
prompt.zh: 一个睡着的病人心率记录为 120 次/分。是哪一类？

label.en: Global: 120 is above the average heart rate of everyone
label.zh: 全局异常：120 高于所有人的平均心率

feedback.en: 120 is perfectly normal during exercise, so by value alone it is not extreme. What makes it odd is the context (asleep).
feedback.zh: 运动时 120 完全正常，光看数值并不极端。让它反常的是上下文（睡着）。

label.en: Collective: a run of high readings
label.zh: 集体异常：一连串偏高的读数

feedback.en: The question describes one reading in a context, not a group that is odd only together.
feedback.zh: 题目描述的是一个上下文里的一个读数，不是只有放在一起才奇怪的一群。

label.en: Contextual: the behavioural attribute (heart rate) is unusual given the contextual one (asleep)
label.zh: 上下文异常：行为属性（心率）在给定上下文属性（睡着）时反常

explain.en: Contextual attribute: state (asleep). Behavioural attribute: heart rate. Same value, different verdict.
explain.zh: 上下文属性：状态（睡着）。行为属性：心率。同一个数值，不同的判决。

title.en: Three settings, and why the task is hard
title.zh: 三种设定，以及为什么这件事难

text.en: What makes anomaly detection different from ordinary classification: anomalies are **rare**, often **unlabelled**, and the next kind of anomaly may look like none you have seen. The settings differ in what labels you have:
text.zh: 异常检测和普通分类不同的地方：异常**很少**，往往**没有标签**，而且下一种异常也许和你见过的都不像。几种设定的区别在于手里有什么标签：

rows.en: train a classifier on expert-labelled samples
rows.zh: 用专家标注的样本训练分类器

rows.en: needs labels of both; classes very imbalanced (boost the anomaly class or make artificial anomalies); cannot detect unknown or emerging anomalies; accuracy is misleading, so aim for recall, which brings false positives
rows.zh: 两类标签都要；类别极不平衡（要加强异常类或造人工异常）；检测不到未知和新出现的异常；准确率会误导，要追求召回，这会带来误报

rows.en: learn what normal looks like; anything outside the learned boundary (high residual, low probability) is flagged
rows.zh: 学“正常”的样子；落在学到的边界之外（残差大、概率低）的就标为异常

rows.en: needs labelled normal data; high false-alarm rate, since a legitimate but unseen record looks like an anomaly
rows.zh: 需要有标签的正常数据；误报率高，因为合法但没见过的记录看上去像异常

rows.en: assume normal objects are clustered in groups with distinct features; an outlier is far from every group; build a profile of normal, flag what differs
rows.zh: 假设正常对象聚成有各自特征的群；离群点离每个群都远；建立“正常”的画像，标出与之不同的

rows.en: normal activity may be diverse and share no pattern, while collective outliers may be very similar to each other; high false-positive rate and still misses real outliers
rows.zh: 正常活动可能很多样、没有共同模式，而集体离群点之间反而很像；误报率高，仍会漏掉真正的离群点

text.en: The rest of the lesson is the **unsupervised** toolbox: four families, each a different answer to *what does “far from normal” mean?*
text.zh: 这一课剩下的是**无监督**的工具箱：四个类别，各自回答*“远离正常”是什么意思*。

head.en: A point is an anomaly if...

rows.en: a model of the normal data gives it low probability
rows.zh: 正常数据的模型给它的概率很低

rows.en: its nearest neighbours are far away
it sits in a region of low density (relative to its neighbours)
rows.zh: 它所在区域的密度低（相对它的邻居）

rows.en: it does not belong strongly to any large, dense cluster
rows.zh: 它不强烈属于任何大而密的簇

title.en: Deeper: why anomalies break standard supervised learning
title.zh: 深入：为什么异常会让标准的监督学习失灵

say.en: A card-fraud data set: 10 000 transactions, 50 of them fraudulent.
say.zh: 一个信用卡欺诈数据集：10000 笔交易，其中 50 笔是欺诈。

say.en: A “classifier” that never flags anything is right on every normal transaction. Its accuracy is 99.5%, and it has caught no fraud at all. Accuracy rewards the majority class.
say.zh: 一个从不报警的“分类器”在所有正常交易上都对。它的准确率是 99.5%，却一笔欺诈也没抓到。准确率奖励的是多数类。

say.en: **Recall** is the share of real anomalies that are caught. For this classifier: 0. The goal is to catch as many anomalies as possible, so recall is the number to watch.
say.zh: **召回率**（recall）是真异常里被抓到的比例。这个分类器：0。目标是尽可能多地抓出异常，所以要看的是召回率。

say.en: Now a detector that catches 80% of the frauds and wrongly flags 2% of the normal transactions, which sounds good.
say.zh: 现在有一个检测器：抓到 80% 的欺诈，同时错误地标出 2% 的正常交易。听上去不错。

say.en: Counts: $TP = 0.8 \times 50 = 40$; $FN = 10$; $FP = 0.02 \times 9950 = 199$ (2% of the normal ones); $TN = 9950 - 199 = 9751$.

**Precision** is the share of alerts that are real. Because normal transactions outnumber frauds 199 to 1, even a 2% false-positive rate buries the 40 true alerts under 199 false ones: about 5 in 6 alerts are false alarms.
say.zh: **精确率**（precision）是警报里真的那部分。因为正常交易比欺诈多 199 倍，即使误报率只有 2%，40 个真警报也会被 199 个假警报淹没：大约六个警报里有五个是误报。

say.en: The useful detector has *lower* accuracy ($97.91\%$) than the useless one ($99.5\%$). Accuracy ranks them backwards.
say.zh: 有用的检测器准确率反而*更低*（$97.91\%$ 对 $99.5\%$）。准确率把两者排反了。

intro.en: Why we do not simply train a classifier on “normal” versus “anomaly”.
intro.zh: 为什么我们不直接训练一个“正常”对“异常”的分类器。

outro.en: So: report **precision and recall** (and their trade-off as the threshold moves), not accuracy; expect false alarms to dominate unless the false-positive rate is tiny; and remember that a supervised model only knows the anomalies in its training set. These pressures are why the other settings exist.
outro.zh: 所以：报告**精确率和召回率**（以及阈值移动时二者的取舍），不要报告准确率；除非误报率极小，否则警报里多半是误报；还要记住，监督模型只认得训练集里出现过的异常。这些压力正是其他设定存在的原因。

title.en: Statistical methods: a model of normal

text.en: **Idea.** Assume the normal data come from a **parametric distribution** $f(\mathbf{x}, \theta)$. Fit it. The density $f(\mathbf{x}, \theta)$ says how likely it is that $\mathbf{x}$ was generated by it: the **smaller**, the more likely $\mathbf{x}$ is an outlier.
text.zh: **想法。**假设正常数据来自某个**参数化分布** $f(\mathbf{x}, \theta)$，把它拟合出来。密度 $f(\mathbf{x}, \theta)$ 表示 $\mathbf{x}$ 由它产生的可能性：**越小**，$\mathbf{x}$ 越可能是离群点。

text.en: The first tool is not a formula but your eyes: a **boxplot** (1-D), **scatter plot** (2-D), **spin plot** (3-D). They are time-consuming and subjective, and stop working beyond three dimensions.
text.zh: 第一个工具不是公式而是眼睛：**箱线图**（1 维）、**散点图**（2 维）、**旋转图**（3 维）。它们耗时又主观，超过三维就没法用了。

text.en: Univariate Gaussian: the z-score
text.zh: 一维高斯：z 分数

text.en: Assume a normal distribution and estimate its parameters by **maximum likelihood** (the Gaussian MLE, the same estimates as in the probability lesson):
text.zh: 假设正态分布，用**最大似然**估计参数（高斯的最大似然估计，和概率那一课里的结果一样）：

text.en: Choose a confidence limit: $\mu \pm 3\sigma$ contains 99.7% of the data. The **z-score** counts how many standard deviations a point is from the mean:
text.zh: 选一个置信界限：$\mu \pm 3\sigma$ 含 99.7% 的数据。**z 分数**数的是一个点离均值有几个标准差：

body.en: Everything depends on the assumption that the data really are (close to) Gaussian. Data with several modes or variable density are hard to model parametrically, and in high dimensions there is too little data to estimate the distribution.
body.zh: 一切都取决于数据确实（接近）高斯这一假设。多峰或密度变化的数据很难用参数分布建模，高维时又没有足够的数据来估计分布。

title.zh: 算例：课件里的温度例子

say.en: Average temperatures. One value, 24.0, is well below the rest.
say.zh: 平均气温。有一个值 24.0 明显低于其他。

say.en: The mean: add up and divide by $N$.
say.zh: 均值：加起来除以 $N$。

say.en: The MLE variance divides by $N$. The squared gaps sum to 23.849, and 24.0 alone contributes $(24 - 28.61)^2 = 21.25$. (The slide prints $\sigma^2 = 2.29$, $\sigma = 1.51$; recomputing from the ten values gives the numbers here.)
say.zh: 最大似然的方差除以 $N$。平方差之和是 23.849，仅 24.0 一项就贡献 $(24 - 28.61)^2 = 21.25$。（课件印的是 $\sigma^2 = 2.29$、$\sigma = 1.51$；从这十个值重算得到的是这里的数。）

say.en: The z-score of the suspect. With the slide's $\sigma = 1.51$ it is 3.05 ($> 3$, flagged); with the exact $\sigma$ it is 2.985, just *under* 3, so the 3-sigma rule does **not** flag it. The next derivation shows why it is so close.
say.zh: 可疑点的 z 分数。用课件的 $\sigma = 1.51$ 是 3.05（$> 3$，被标出）；用精确的 $\sigma$ 是 2.985，刚好*低于* 3，3σ 规则**不会**标出它。下一段推导说明为什么这么接近。

say.en: All other values are within about half a standard deviation of the mean: 24.0 is the only candidate. The lecture's conclusion (24 is an anomaly) is the intended reading; what a marker wants to see is $\mu$, $\sigma$, $z$ and the comparison with 3.
say.zh: 其余值都在均值附近约半个标准差以内：24.0 是唯一的候选。课件的结论（24 是异常）是出题的本意；评分要看到的是 $\mu$、$\sigma$、$z$ 以及和 3 的比较。

title.en: Deeper: a 3-sigma rule that can never fire
title.zh: 深入：永远触发不了的 3σ 规则

say.en: Single out the point with the biggest gap $d$. Deviations from the mean always sum to zero, so the other $N - 1$ deviations sum to $-d$.
say.zh: 挑出离得最远的那个点，偏差为 $d$。离均值的偏差之和总是 0，所以其余 $N - 1$ 个偏差之和是 $-d$。

say.en: For fixed total, the sum of squares is smallest when the $N - 1$ numbers are equal (Cauchy-Schwarz). So the others contribute at least $d^2/(N-1)$ to the variance.
say.zh: 总和固定时，这 $N - 1$ 个数全相等，平方和最小（柯西—施瓦茨）。所以其余点至少给方差贡献 $d^2/(N-1)$。

say.en: Add the point's own $d^2$: the total squared deviation $N\sigma^2$ is at least $\frac{N}{N-1}d^2$.
say.zh: 加上这个点自己的 $d^2$：总平方偏差 $N\sigma^2$ 至少是 $\frac{N}{N-1}d^2$。

say.en: Rearranged: **no single point can be more than $\sqrt{N-1}$ standard deviations from the mean.** An outlier inflates the very $\sigma$ it is measured with.
say.zh: 整理得：**任何单个点离均值都不会超过 $\sqrt{N-1}$ 个标准差。**离群点会把用来衡量它的 $\sigma$ 自己撑大。

say.en: With $\sigma$ as the MLE: for ten points the 3-sigma rule **can never flag anything**. The slide's $z = 3.04$ is impossible for ten points; the true value 2.985 is almost at the ceiling of 3, because 24.0 is as extreme as ten points allow. (With the sample standard deviation, dividing by $N - 1$, the ceiling is $(N-1)/\sqrt N = 2.85$.)
say.zh: $\sigma$ 取最大似然估计时：十个点的 3σ 规则**永远标不出任何点**。课件里的 $z = 3.04$ 对十个点是不可能的；真实值 2.985 几乎已顶到 3 这个上限，因为 24.0 已是十个点所允许的极端。（用样本标准差，即除以 $N - 1$，上限是 $(N-1)/\sqrt N = 2.85$。）

say.en: **Grubbs' test** uses the statistic $G = \max_i |x_i - \mu| / \sigma$ (here with the sample standard deviation $s = 1.628$) but compares it with a critical value that **depends on $N$** (about 2.29 at the 5% level for $N = 10$, from tables). $G = 2.83 > 2.29$: 24.0 is declared an outlier. For a single outlier in roughly normal data, this is the properly calibrated version of the z-score.
say.zh: **Grubbs 检验**用的统计量是 $G = \max_i |x_i - \mu| / \sigma$（这里取样本标准差 $s = 1.628$），但拿它和一个**依赖 $N$** 的临界值比较（$N = 10$、5% 水平约为 2.29，查表得）。$G = 2.83 > 2.29$：24.0 被判为离群点。对近似正态数据里的单个离群点，这是校准得当的 z 分数。

intro.en: The slide's example sits suspiciously close to $z = 3$. There is a reason.
intro.zh: 课件的例子离 $z = 3$ 近得可疑。这是有原因的。

text.en: With several features, assume a **multivariate normal** distribution: a mean vector $\boldsymbol\mu$ and a covariance matrix $\Sigma$ (for two features $\Sigma = \begin{pmatrix}\sigma(x,x) & \sigma(x,y)\\ \sigma(y,x) & \sigma(y,y)\end{pmatrix}$: variances on the diagonal, how the features vary together off it). The **Mahalanobis distance** measures how far a point is from the mean *in units of the data's own spread, in every direction*:
text.zh: 有多个特征时，假设**多元正态分布**：均值向量 $\boldsymbol\mu$ 和协方差矩阵 $\Sigma$（两个特征时 $\Sigma = \begin{pmatrix}\sigma(x,x) & \sigma(x,y)\\ \sigma(y,x) & \sigma(y,y)\end{pmatrix}$：对角线是方差，非对角线是两个特征如何一起变化）。**马氏距离**（Mahalanobis distance）衡量一个点离均值多远，*单位是数据在每个方向上自己的散布*：

text.en: Read $\Sigma^{-1}$ as a rescaling: a gap along a direction in which the data vary a lot costs little; a gap across the data's narrow direction costs a lot. In one dimension $D_M = |x - \mu|/\sigma$, the z-score. A large $D_M$ means the point is unlikely under the distribution: a potential outlier.
text.zh: 把 $\Sigma^{-1}$ 看作一次重新标度：沿着数据变化大的方向偏离，代价小；横着数据窄的方向偏离，代价大。一维时 $D_M = |x - \mu|/\sigma$，就是 z 分数。$D_M$ 大，说明这个点在该分布下不太可能：潜在的离群点。

caption.en: Equal Euclidean distance, very different Mahalanobis distance.
caption.zh: 欧氏距离相同，马氏距离差很多。

text.en: The slide's scatter plot makes the same point with numbers: a point A at Euclidean distance 5.7 has Mahalanobis distance 5.9 ($\sqrt{35}$), while B, *farther* in Euclidean terms (7.1), has Mahalanobis distance only 4.9 ($\sqrt{24}$): B lies along the cloud's long axis, where large values are common.
text.zh: 课件的散点图用数字说明同一件事：点 A 欧氏距离 5.7，马氏距离 5.9（$\sqrt{35}$）；而欧氏距离*更远*的 B（7.1），马氏距离只有 4.9（$\sqrt{24}$）：B 在点云的长轴方向上，那里出现大值很常见。

text.en: Grubbs' test on the distances
text.zh: 对距离做 Grubbs 检验

text.en: The Mahalanobis distances turn many features into one number per point. Treat that set of numbers as (roughly) normal and apply **Grubbs' test** to find a single univariate outlier: $G = \max_i |x_i - \mu|/\sigma$, as in the last page, compared with a critical value that depends on the number of points.
text.zh: 马氏距离把许多特征变成每个点一个数。把这组数当作（近似）正态，用 **Grubbs 检验**找出单个一元离群点：$G = \max_i |x_i - \mu|/\sigma$，和上一页一样，并与一个依赖点数的临界值比较。

body.en: Mahalanobis distance is mainly useful for **global** anomalies. It is much less effective for local, contextual or collective ones, because one Gaussian describes the whole data set.
body.zh: 马氏距离主要对**全局**异常有用。对局部、上下文或集体异常效果差得多，因为一个高斯分布描述的是整个数据集。

text.en: Statistical methods: pros and cons
text.zh: 统计方法：优点与缺点

rows.en: Well understood and well validated tests
rows.zh: 检验方法成熟、经过充分验证

rows.en: Data may be hard to model parametrically (several modes, variable density)
rows.zh: 数据可能很难参数化建模（多峰、密度变化）

rows.en: A quantitative degree of outlierness (a score)
rows.zh: 给出异常程度的定量度量（一个分数）

rows.en: In high dimensions there may be too little data to estimate the distribution
rows.zh: 高维时可能没有足够数据来估计分布

title.zh: 算例：欧氏距离与马氏距离

say.en: Two features with variance 1 and correlation 0.8: when one is large, the other tends to be large too (the tilted cloud). A = (2, 2) and B = (2, -2).
say.zh: 两个特征，方差都为 1，相关系数 0.8：一个大时另一个也倾向于大（倾斜的点云）。A = (2, 2)，B = (2, −2)。

say.en: Invert the $2 \times 2$ matrix: swap the diagonal, negate the off-diagonal, divide by the determinant $1 - 0.64 = 0.36$.
say.zh: 求 $2 \times 2$ 矩阵的逆：交换对角线、非对角线取负、除以行列式 $1 - 0.64 = 0.36$。

say.en: By plain distance the two points are equally far from the mean.
say.zh: 按普通距离，两点离均值一样远。

say.en: Expand $\mathbf{x}^\top\Sigma^{-1}\mathbf{x} = (x^2 - 1.6xy + y^2)/0.36$. For $(2, 2)$ the cross term *cancels* part of the squares: moving along the correlation is cheap.
say.zh: 展开 $\mathbf{x}^\top\Sigma^{-1}\mathbf{x} = (x^2 - 1.6xy + y^2)/0.36$。对 $(2, 2)$，交叉项*抵消*了一部分平方项：顺着相关方向走代价小。

say.en: For $(2, -2)$ the cross term *adds*: going against the correlation is expensive.
say.zh: 对 $(2, -2)$，交叉项是*加上去*的：逆着相关方向走代价大。

say.en: Why: the covariance has two principal directions. Along $(1, 1)$ the variance is 1.8, along $(1, -1)$ only 0.2. $D_M^2$ divides each squared gap by the variance of its direction: A is entirely along the wide direction, B entirely along the narrow one.
say.zh: 原因：协方差有两个主方向。沿 $(1, 1)$ 方差是 1.8，沿 $(1, -1)$ 只有 0.2。$D_M^2$ 把每个方向上的平方偏差除以该方向的方差：A 完全在宽的方向上，B 完全在窄的方向上。

text.en: **Idea.** An object is an anomaly if its nearest neighbours are far away: its proximity deviates from the proximity of most other objects. No distribution needed; defining a distance is easier than finding a distribution.
text.zh: **想法。**如果一个对象的最近邻很远，它就是异常：它的邻近程度与其他大多数对象很不一样。不需要分布；定义一个距离比找出一个分布容易。

text.en: **Common score:** the distance to the $k$-th nearest neighbour. The score is sensitive to $k$. Eight 1-D points, a tight group of six and a pair of anomalies at 8.0 and 8.3:
text.zh: **常用分数：**到第 $k$ 个最近邻的距离。分数对 $k$ 很敏感。八个一维点：紧凑的六个点，加上位于 8.0 和 8.3 的一对异常点：

text.en: With $k = 1$ the pair protects itself: each is the other's nearest neighbour at 0.3, hardly worse than the normal 0.2, so **nothing** is flagged. With $k = 2$ the scores jump to 6.0 and 6.3. $k$ must exceed the size of any group of anomalies you want to find (a collective anomaly of $m$ points hides at $k < m$), but a $k$ that is too big mixes in other groups.
text.zh: $k = 1$ 时这一对互相保护：每个是对方的最近邻，距离 0.3，只比正常的 0.2 略大，所以**一个都标不出来**。$k = 2$ 时分数跳到 6.0 和 6.3。$k$ 必须大于你想找的任一异常群的大小（$m$ 个点的集体异常在 $k < m$ 时藏得住），但 $k$ 太大又会混进别的群。

text.en: Proximity: pros and cons
text.zh: 邻近方法：优点与缺点

rows.en: A proximity measure is easier to define than a distribution
rows.zh: 邻近度量比分布更容易定义

rows.en: Does **not** work well if the data have widely variable density
rows.zh: 数据密度差别很大时**不**好用

title.en: Why one global threshold fails when densities differ
title.zh: 为什么密度不一时一个全局阈值会失效

alt.zh: 网格上的九个点。左下方四个稠密的点 A、B、C、D；右边四个分散的稀疏点 E、F、G、H；中间的点 I，用虚线连到它最近的两个邻居 B 和 D。

text.en: Distance to the 2nd nearest neighbour (Manhattan distance $|\Delta x| + |\Delta y|$):
text.zh: 到第 2 个最近邻的距离（曼哈顿距离 $|\Delta x| + |\Delta y|$）：

text.en: I is the anomaly to the eye: its neighbours are about 5 away while the dense group's are 1-2 apart. But its score (5) is **lower** than that of every sparse point (6), who are perfectly normal for their group. A threshold that catches I (say, above 4) flags all of E-H as well; a threshold that spares E-H (above 6) lets I through. **No single threshold separates them.** A distance only means something relative to the local scale.
text.zh: 在眼里 I 就是异常：它的邻居约 5 远，而稠密群里的点彼此只相距 1–2。可是它的分数（5）比每个稀疏点（6）都**低**，而稀疏点在它们那一群里完全正常。能抓住 I 的阈值（比如大于 4）也会把 E–H 全标出来；能放过 E–H 的阈值（大于 6）又会放过 I。**没有一个阈值能把它们分开。**距离只有相对局部的尺度才有意义。

text.en: The same failure hits the statistical Gaussian (one distribution cannot fit two scales) and the basic density score. The fix: compare each point with *its own neighbourhood*.
text.zh: 同样的失败也会落到统计的高斯方法（一个分布装不下两个尺度）和基本的密度分数上。补救办法：把每个点和*它自己的邻域*比。

prompt.en: Which is the best summary of why a global kNN-distance threshold fails here?
prompt.zh: 下面哪句最好地总结了为什么全局的 kNN 距离阈值在这里失效？

label.en: Normal points in a sparse group have larger kNN distances than an anomaly next to a dense group
label.zh: 稀疏群里的正常点，其 kNN 距离比紧挨着稠密群的异常点还大

label.en: The Manhattan distance is the wrong metric; Euclidean distance would fix it
label.zh: 曼哈顿距离选错了；换欧氏距离就好了

feedback.en: Changing the metric rescales distances but both groups keep their different scales; the ordering problem remains.
feedback.zh: 换度量只会重新标度距离，两群的尺度差别依然在，排序问题还在。

label.en: $k = 2$ is too small; with $k = 8$ it works

feedback.en: A larger $k$ makes distances bigger everywhere and does not remove the difference of scale between the two groups.
feedback.zh: 更大的 $k$ 让所有距离都变大，两群的尺度差别并没有消除。

explain.en: The absolute distance conflates “far” with “in a sparse region”. Relative density (LOF) separates them.
explain.zh: 绝对距离把“远”和“在稀疏区域”混为一谈。相对密度（LOF）把它们分开。

title.zh: 基于密度：先绝对，再相对（LOF）

text.en: **Idea.** Outliers are objects in regions of **low density**: the outlier score rises as the density around a point falls. Two simple densities: count the points within a fixed radius $d$; or take the **inverse of the mean distance to the $k$ nearest neighbours**:
text.zh: **想法。**离群点是处在**低密度**区域的对象：一个点周围的密度越低，异常分数越高。两个简单的密度：数固定半径 $d$ 内的点数；或者取**到 $k$ 个最近邻的平均距离的倒数**：

text.en: $N(\mathbf{x}, k)$ is the set of the $k$ nearest neighbours of $\mathbf{x}$. Short distances mean high density. **Limitation:** these are *absolute* densities, so with variable density they fail exactly as in the last page.
text.zh: $N(\mathbf{x}, k)$ 是 $\mathbf{x}$ 的 $k$ 个最近邻的集合。距离短就是密度高。**局限：**这是*绝对*密度，所以在密度变化时会像上一页那样失败。

text.en: **Local density (the Local Outlier Factor idea).** Compare each point's density with the average density of **its own neighbours**. The lecture's version:
text.zh: **局部密度（局部离群因子 LOF 的想法）。**把每个点的密度和**它自己邻居**的平均密度比。课件的版本：

blocks.tex: \text{relative density}(\mathbf{x}, k) = \left(\frac{\text{density}(\mathbf{x}, k)}{\frac1k\sum_{\mathbf{y}\in N(\mathbf{x}, k)}\text{density}(\mathbf{y}, k)}\right)^{-1}

text.en: Read it: own density divided by the neighbours' average density, **inverted**. So the score is $\bar\rho_{\text{neighbours}}/\rho_{\mathbf{x}}$:
text.zh: 读法：自己的密度除以邻居的平均密度，再**取倒数**。所以分数是 $\bar\rho_{\text{邻居}}/\rho_{\mathbf{x}}$：

items.en: $\approx 1$: as dense as the neighbours, normal;
items.zh: $\approx 1$：和邻居一样密，正常；

items.en: $\gg 1$: much sparser than the neighbours, an outlier, **even if the area is not low-density globally**;
items.zh: $\gg 1$：比邻居稀疏得多，是离群点，**即使这一带在全局上并不是低密度**；

items.en: $< 1$: denser than the neighbours (inside a cluster).
items.zh: $< 1$：比邻居更密（在簇的内部）。

text.en: The original LOF, with reachability distance
text.zh: 原始的 LOF：用可达距离

text.en: Breunig et al. (2000) smooth the distances. For a point $p$ and a number $k$:
text.zh: Breunig 等人（2000）把距离做了平滑。对一个点 $p$ 和一个数 $k$：

items.en: **$k$-distance** $d_k(p)$: the distance from $p$ to its $k$-th nearest neighbour; $N_k(p)$ the points within it (at least $k$, more with ties).
items.zh: **$k$-距离** $d_k(p)$：$p$ 到其第 $k$ 个最近邻的距离；$N_k(p)$ 是在这个距离之内的点（至少 $k$ 个，有并列时更多）。

items.en: **Reachability distance** $\text{reach}_k(p, o) = \max\{d_k(o),\; d(p, o)\}$: the true distance, but never less than $o$'s own $k$-distance (so points inside a tight cluster all look equally far from each other, which stabilises the score).
items.zh: **可达距离** $\text{reach}_k(p, o) = \max\{d_k(o),\; d(p, o)\}$：真实距离，但不小于 $o$ 自己的 $k$-距离（于是紧簇内的点彼此看起来一样远，让分数更稳定）。

items.en: **Local reachability density** $\text{lrd}_k(p) = \Bigl(\frac{1}{|N_k(p)|}\sum_{o \in N_k(p)}\text{reach}_k(p, o)\Bigr)^{-1}$: the inverse of the mean reachability distance.
items.zh: **局部可达密度** $\text{lrd}_k(p) = \Bigl(\frac{1}{|N_k(p)|}\sum_{o \in N_k(p)}\text{reach}_k(p, o)\Bigr)^{-1}$：平均可达距离的倒数。

items.en: **LOF** $\text{LOF}_k(p) = \dfrac{1}{|N_k(p)|}\sum_{o \in N_k(p)}\dfrac{\text{lrd}_k(o)}{\text{lrd}_k(p)}$: the neighbours' density over $p$'s own.
items.zh: **LOF** $\text{LOF}_k(p) = \dfrac{1}{|N_k(p)|}\sum_{o \in N_k(p)}\dfrac{\text{lrd}_k(o)}{\text{lrd}_k(p)}$：邻居的密度除以 $p$ 自己的密度。

text.en: The lecture's score is the same idea with plain distances instead of reachability distances. Both: $\approx 1$ normal, $\gg 1$ outlier.
text.zh: 课件的分数是同一个想法，只是用普通距离代替可达距离。两者：$\approx 1$ 正常，$\gg 1$ 离群。

text.en: Density: pros and cons
text.zh: 密度方法：优点与缺点

rows.en: Works even if the data have variable density (the relative version)
rows.zh: 数据密度变化时也好用（相对版本）
要选参数：$k$（邻居数）或 $d$（半径）

title.zh: 算例：课件的一维例子（2 近邻，曼哈顿距离）

say.en: The 20 values of the slide: a tight group of ten at 1-1.5 and a loose spread from 4.55 on. Score the two query points $x = 0.5$ and $x = 4$ (not in $D$) with $k = 2$.
say.zh: 课件的 20 个值：1–1.5 有十个点的紧簇，4.55 往后是松散的分布。对两个查询点 $x = 0.5$ 和 $x = 4$（不在 $D$ 里）用 $k = 2$ 打分。

say.en: The two nearest points to 0.5 are 1 (distance 0.5) and 1.05 (0.55). The mean distance is 0.525; density is its inverse (the slide's 1.9).
say.zh: 离 0.5 最近的两点是 1（距离 0.5）和 1.05（0.55）。平均距离 0.525；密度是它的倒数（课件的 1.9）。

say.en: The neighbours' own densities. Point 1 has neighbours 1.05 and 1.1; point 1.05 has neighbours 1 and 1.1. Both sit in the tight group, so their densities are high.
say.zh: 邻居自己的密度。点 1 的邻居是 1.05 和 1.1；点 1.05 的邻居是 1 和 1.1。两者都在紧簇里，所以密度很高。

say.en: Mean neighbour density over own density (the inverse of the slide's “relative density”). 0.5 is about **8.75 times sparser** than its neighbours. (The slide prints 9.1; rounding the densities does not give that, so 8.75 is the correct value. Either way, far above 1.)
say.zh: 邻居平均密度除以自己的密度（课件“相对密度”的倒数）。0.5 比它的邻居**稀疏约 8.75 倍**。（课件印的是 9.1；把密度四舍五入也得不到这个数，所以 8.75 才是对的。无论哪个，都远大于 1。）

say.en: For 4: the nearest points are 4.55 (0.55) and 5.6 (1.6).
Neighbour 4.55 has neighbours 5.6 and 6.8; neighbour 5.6 has 4.55 and 6.8. Both are in the loose region, so their densities are low (0.61 and 0.89).
say.zh: 邻居 4.55 的邻居是 5.6 和 6.8；邻居 5.6 的邻居是 4.55 和 6.8。两者都在松散的区域，所以密度很低（0.61 和 0.89）。

say.en: Score about 0.80 (the slide: 0.81, from rounded values). Below 1: 4 is about as dense as its neighbours, in a region where every point is far from every other. **Not an outlier**, although its absolute distances (0.55, 1.6) are much larger than 0.5's.
say.zh: 分数约 0.80（课件：0.81，由四舍五入的值得到）。小于 1：4 和它的邻居差不多一样密，处在一个每个点离其他点都很远的区域。**不是离群点**，尽管它的绝对距离（0.55、1.6）比 0.5 的大得多。

intro.en: Same recipe as the formula above, with every number computed.
intro.zh: 套上面的公式，每个数都算出来。

outro.en: The point of the example: 0.5 is next to a dense group, so it is an outlier **relative to its neighbourhood** (score 8.75); 4 has larger absolute distances but sits in a sparse region where that is normal (0.80).
outro.zh: 例子的要点：0.5 紧挨着一个稠密群，所以**相对它的邻域**是离群点（8.75）；4 的绝对距离更大，但处在稀疏区域，那里这样是正常的（0.80）。

title.en: Worked: a full LOF by hand (k = 2)
title.zh: 算例：手算一个完整的 LOF（k = 2）

say.en: The points of the figure; Manhattan distance, $k = 2$. We compute $\text{LOF}(I)$, which needs the neighbours of $I$, then their neighbours. (The sparse group is $E(10,6), F(14,4), G(12,0), H(10,0)$.)
say.zh: 图里的点；曼哈顿距离，$k = 2$。我们算 $\text{LOF}(I)$，这要用到 $I$ 的邻居，再用到它们的邻居。（稀疏群是 $E(10,6), F(14,4), G(12,0), H(10,0)$。）

say.en: Distances from $I$ to the dense group: $|5-2| + |2-0| = 5$ to B, $4 + 1 = 5$ to D, 6 to A and C; to the sparse group it is at least 9. The two nearest are B and D, so $d_2(I) = 5$.
say.zh: $I$ 到稠密群的距离：到 B 是 $|5-2| + |2-0| = 5$，到 D 是 $4 + 1 = 5$，到 A 和 C 是 6；到稀疏群至少 9。最近的两个是 B 和 D，所以 $d_2(I) = 5$。

say.en: The $k$-distances of the neighbours: B has C at distance 1 and D at 2, so $d_2(B) = 2$. D has A and C both at distance 1, so $d_2(D) = 1$.
say.zh: 邻居的 $k$-距离：B 到 C 是 1，到 D 是 2，所以 $d_2(B) = 2$。D 到 A、C 都是 1，所以 $d_2(D) = 1$。

say.en: Reachability distances from $I$: the larger of the neighbour's own $k$-distance and the true distance. Here the true distance (5) wins.
say.zh: 从 $I$ 出发的可达距离：邻居自己的 $k$-距离与真实距离中较大的那个。这里是真实距离（5）较大。

say.en: Local reachability density: the number of neighbours over the sum of reachability distances (the inverse of their mean).
say.zh: 局部可达密度：邻居数除以可达距离之和（即平均值的倒数）。

say.en: The neighbours are $\tfrac{2/3}{1/5} = 3.3$ times denser than $I$: a clear outlier.
say.zh: 邻居的密度是 $I$ 的 $\tfrac{2/3}{1/5} = 3.3$ 倍：明显的离群点。

say.en: The same steps for the others: every dense point has $\text{lrd} = 2/3$ and every sparse point $1/6$, each equal to its neighbours', so LOF is 1 for all eight. Compare the plain 2-distances (2, 2, 1, 1 | 6, 6, 6, 6 | 5): they would rank $I$ *below* the sparse points; LOF ranks it first.
say.zh: 对其他点做同样的步骤：每个稠密点的 lrd 是 $2/3$，每个稀疏点是 $1/6$，都和各自邻居的一样，所以八个点的 LOF 都是 1。对比普通的 2-距离（2, 2, 1, 1 | 6, 6, 6, 6 | 5）：它会把 $I$ 排在稀疏点*之后*；LOF 把它排在第一。

prompt.en: The local reachability density of $I$: the number of neighbours over the sum of the two reachability distances.
prompt.zh: $I$ 的局部可达密度：邻居数除以两个可达距离之和。

title.en: Clustering-based: do you belong to a big cluster?
title.zh: 基于聚类：你属于某个大簇吗？

text.en: **Idea.** Normal data belong to **large, dense clusters**. Outliers are objects that do not strongly belong to any cluster: they are far from every cluster centre, or they form a **small** cluster of their own (which extends the idea from single objects to groups). Cluster first, then score by cluster structure. The lecture's method, **CBLOF** (cluster-based local outlier factor):
text.zh: **想法。**正常数据属于**大而密的簇**。离群点是不强烈属于任何簇的对象：离每个簇中心都很远，或者自己组成一个**小**簇（这把“离群”的概念从单个对象推广到了群）。先聚类，再按簇的结构打分。课件的方法是 **CBLOF**（基于聚类的局部离群因子）：

items.en: **Cluster** the data (e.g. k-means, Euclidean distance).
items.zh: 对数据**聚类**（如 k-means，欧氏距离）。

items.en: **Label clusters large or small.** Sort the clusters by size. Large clusters ($LC$) hold most of the data; small clusters ($SC$) few points. Two parameters: $\alpha$, a cumulative size threshold (e.g. 90% of the points), and $\beta$, a minimum size ratio between consecutive clusters (e.g. $5\times$). The large clusters are the biggest ones $C_1..C_b$ such that together they hold at least $\alpha$ of the points, or $|C_b|/|C_{b+1}| \ge \beta$.
items.zh: **把簇标成大或小。**按大小给簇排序。大簇（$LC$）装了大部分数据；小簇（$SC$）只有少数点。两个参数：$\alpha$，累计大小阈值（如 90% 的点）；$\beta$，相邻簇之间的最小大小比（如 $5$ 倍）。大簇是最大的那几个 $C_1..C_b$，使它们合起来至少含 $\alpha$ 的点，或 $|C_b|/|C_{b+1}| \ge \beta$。

items.en: **Score** each point $t$ (formula below).
items.zh: 给每个点 $t$ **打分**（公式见下）。

items.en: **High CBLOF means high anomaly likelihood.**
items.zh: **CBLOF 高，异常的可能性高。**

blocks.tex: \text{CBLOF}(t) = \begin{cases} |C_i|\cdot\text{distance}(t, C_i) & \text{if } C_i \in LC \;(t \in C_i)\\[2pt] |C_i|\cdot\min_{C_j \in LC}\text{distance}(t, C_j) & \text{if } C_i \in SC \;(t \in C_i)\end{cases}

text.en: For a point in a large cluster: the cluster's size times its distance to its own cluster (centre). For a point in a small cluster: its cluster's size times the distance to the *nearest large cluster*. Points in small isolated clusters, and distant points in large clusters, are flagged.
text.zh: 大簇里的点：该簇的大小乘以到自己所在簇（中心）的距离。小簇里的点：该簇的大小乘以到*最近的大簇*的距离。小而孤立的簇里的点，以及大簇里的远点，会被标出。

text.en: Another formulation: two-phase filtering
text.zh: 另一种做法：两阶段过滤

items.en: **Point-level filtering:** iteratively remove points whose removal improves the clustering quality most: individual anomalies.
items.zh: **点级过滤：**迭代地去掉对聚类质量改善最大的点：个体异常。

items.en: **Cluster-level filtering:** discard small clusters far from the others: group anomalies.
items.zh: **簇级过滤：**丢弃离其他簇很远的小簇：群体异常。

text.en: Clustering: pros and cons
text.zh: 聚类方法：优点与缺点

rows.en: Needs thresholds for large versus small clusters ($\alpha$, $\beta$)
Extends the notion of outlier from single objects to groups
rows.zh: 把离群的概念从单个对象推广到群

rows.en: Sensitive to the number of clusters chosen
Outliers may distort the clusters they are found with (they pull a k-means centre)
rows.zh: 离群点可能扭曲聚类本身（把 k-means 的中心拉歪）

say.en: Three k-means clusters, sorted by size.
say.zh: 三个 k-means 簇，按大小排序。

say.en: Cumulative size: $C_1$ alone holds 62.5%, below $\alpha$; $C_1$ and $C_2$ together hold 93.75%, above it. The size ratio $|C_2|/|C_3| = 5 \ge \beta$ also marks the break. So $LC = \{C_1, C_2\}$ and $SC = \{C_3\}$.
say.zh: 累计大小：$C_1$ 自己占 62.5%，低于 $\alpha$；$C_1$ 和 $C_2$ 合起来占 93.75%，超过了。大小比 $|C_2|/|C_3| = 5 \ge \beta$ 也标出了断点。于是 $LC = \{C_1, C_2\}$，$SC = \{C_3\}$。

say.en: A point of the small cluster, whose distances to the centres of $C_1$ and $C_2$ are 9.0 and 6.0: size of its cluster times the *nearest large cluster's* distance.
say.zh: 小簇里的点，它到 $C_1$、$C_2$ 中心的距离分别是 9.0 和 6.0：它所在簇的大小乘以*最近大簇*的距离。

say.en: A far-out point of a large cluster: its cluster's size times the distance to its own centre.
say.zh: 大簇里的一个远点：它所在簇的大小乘以到自己簇中心的距离。

say.en: A typical point of $C_2$.
say.zh: $C_2$ 里的一个典型点。

say.en: Both $t_1$ and $t_2$ score above the typical point $t_3$. Notice the size factor: it makes far points of big clusters score very high. The slide's own plot shows it: the small cluster's points score about 31-32 while far-out points of the large clusters score 185-564. Read the scores by comparing them, not by a fixed meaning of “small cluster = high score”.
say.zh: $t_1$ 和 $t_2$ 的分数都高于典型点 $t_3$。注意大小这个因子：它让大簇里的远点分数非常高。课件自己的图就是这样：小簇的点约 31–32，而大簇里的远点是 185–564。读这些分数要靠相互比较，而不是认定“小簇 = 高分”。

title.en: The four families side by side

rows.en: normal data from a parametric distribution
rows.zh: 正常数据来自参数分布

rows.en: wrong if the model assumption is wrong; multi-modal, variable density; high dimension
rows.zh: 模型假设错了就错；多峰、密度变化；高维

rows.en: outliers are far from their neighbours

rows.zh: 到第 $k$ 个最近邻的距离

rows.en: outliers sit in low-density regions, relative to neighbours
rows.zh: 离群点在低密度区域，相对邻居而言

rows.en: normal data are in large dense clusters
rows.zh: 正常数据在大而密的簇里

rows.en: thresholds; number of clusters; outliers distort clusters
rows.zh: 阈值；簇数；离群点扭曲聚类

prompt.en: Which family is best suited to this data: one tight cluster of 500 sensor readings and another loose cluster of 500, plus a few points just outside the tight cluster?
prompt.zh: 下面这份数据最适合哪类方法：500 个传感器读数组成的一个紧簇，另一个 500 个读数组成的松散簇，再加几个刚好在紧簇外面的点？

label.en: Distance to the $k$-th neighbour with one global threshold
label.zh: 到第 $k$ 个邻居的距离，用一个全局阈值

feedback.en: The loose cluster's normal points would have larger distances than the points just outside the tight one: no threshold works.
feedback.zh: 松散簇的正常点，距离会比紧簇外的那几个点还大：没有任何阈值行得通。

label.zh: 一个高斯分布加 z 分数

feedback.en: Two clusters of different spread are not one Gaussian; the fitted $\sigma$ would be large and swallow the points.
feedback.zh: 两个散布不同的簇不是一个高斯；拟合出的 $\sigma$ 会很大，把那几个点吞掉。

label.en: Local relative density (LOF): compare each point with its own neighbourhood
label.zh: 局部相对密度（LOF）：把每个点和它自己的邻域比

explain.en: Variable density is exactly what relative density was designed for.
explain.zh: 密度变化正是相对密度被设计出来要处理的情形。

prompt.en: A data set has 5,000 transactions, of which 50 are fraud. A detector catches 80% of the frauds and wrongly flags 2% of the normal transactions. What is its precision? Give a decimal to three places.
prompt.zh: 一个数据集有 5,000 笔交易，其中 50 笔是欺诈。一个检测器抓到 80% 的欺诈，同时错误地标出 2% 的正常交易。它的精确率是多少？保留三位小数。

explain.en: $TP = 0.8 \times 50 = 40$. The normal ones number $4950$, so $FP = 0.02 \times 4950 = 99$. Precision $= 40/(40 + 99) = 0.288$: about 7 in 10 alerts are false.

prompt.en: Data $D = \{1.0, 1.1, 1.3, 1.5, 5.0, 5.6, 6.4, 7.4\}$. Using the lecture's method with $k = 2$ (density = inverse of the mean distance to the 2 nearest neighbours; score = mean density of the neighbours divided by the point's own density), score the query point $x = 2.4$. Two decimals.
prompt.zh: 数据 $D = \{1.0, 1.1, 1.3, 1.5, 5.0, 5.6, 6.4, 7.4\}$。用课件的方法，$k = 2$（密度 = 到 2 个最近邻的平均距离的倒数；分数 = 邻居的平均密度除以该点自己的密度），给查询点 $x = 2.4$ 打分。保留两位小数。

explain.en: Nearest to 2.4: 1.5 (0.9) and 1.3 (1.1); mean 1.0, density 1.00. Neighbour 1.5 has neighbours 1.3 (0.2) and 1.1 (0.4): density 3.33. Neighbour 1.3 has 1.1 (0.2) and 1.5 (0.2): density 5.00. Mean neighbour density $(3.33 + 5.00)/2$ divided by 1.00 gives $4.17$: 2.4 is much sparser than its neighbours, an outlier.

prompt.en: Two features with mean $(0, 0)$ and covariance $\Sigma = \begin{pmatrix}4 & 0\\0 & 1\end{pmatrix}$. Find the Mahalanobis distance of the point $(4, 2)$. Two decimals.
prompt.zh: 两个特征，均值 $(0, 0)$，协方差 $\Sigma = \begin{pmatrix}4 & 0\\0 & 1\end{pmatrix}$。求点 $(4, 2)$ 的马氏距离。保留两位小数。

explain.en: $\Sigma$ is diagonal, so $\Sigma^{-1} = \text{diag}(1/4, 1)$ and $D_M^2 = 4^2/4 + 2^2/1 = 4 + 4 = 8$, $D_M = \sqrt 8 = 2.83$. (The Euclidean distance would be $\sqrt{20} = 4.47$: dividing by the variances shrinks the first feature's gap.)
explain.zh: $\Sigma$ 是对角的，所以 $\Sigma^{-1} = \text{diag}(1/4, 1)$，$D_M^2 = 4^2/4 + 2^2/1 = 4 + 4 = 8$，$D_M = \sqrt 8 = 2.83$。（欧氏距离是 $\sqrt{20} = 4.47$：除以方差把第一个特征的偏差缩小了。）

prompt.en: A bank has years of transactions that it is confident are legitimate, but almost no confirmed fraud examples, and fraud tactics keep changing. Which approach fits, and what is its main risk?
prompt.zh: 一家银行有多年被确认合法的交易记录，但几乎没有确认的欺诈样本，而且欺诈手法一直在变。哪种方法合适，主要风险是什么？

label.en: Semi-supervised: learn a model of normal transactions and flag departures; the risk is false alarms on legitimate but unseen behaviour
label.zh: 半监督：学一个正常交易的模型，把偏离的标出来；风险是对合法但没见过的行为误报

label.en: Supervised: train a classifier of fraud versus legitimate; the risk is none, since the data is plentiful
label.zh: 监督：训练欺诈对合法的分类器；没有风险，因为数据很多

feedback.en: There are almost no fraud labels, and a supervised model cannot detect new tactics it has not seen; classes would be extremely imbalanced.
feedback.zh: 几乎没有欺诈标签，监督模型也检测不到没见过的新手法；类别会极端不平衡。

label.en: Unsupervised: ignore the legitimacy labels because labels never help
label.zh: 无监督：忽略合法的标签，因为标签从来没用

feedback.en: Knowing that the data is (almost) all normal is valuable: it lets us model normal directly instead of guessing it from mixed data.
feedback.zh: 知道数据（几乎）全是正常的很有价值：可以直接给正常建模，而不是在混合的数据里去猜。

label.en: Supervised, but using accuracy to evaluate

feedback.en: Accuracy is misleading when anomalies are rare: always saying “normal” scores about 99.5%.
feedback.zh: 异常很少时准确率会误导：永远回答“正常”也能得约 99.5%。

explain.en: Labels only for the normal class is the semi-supervised setting; its challenge is false alarms from legitimate novelty.
explain.zh: 只有正常类的标签，是半监督设定；它的挑战是合法的新情况造成的误报。

title.zh: 评估异常检测器（A 部分）

prompt.en: A detector for rare anomalies (0.5% of the data) reaches 99.3% accuracy. Explain why this number may be misleading, and which metrics you would report instead. (2-3 lines)
prompt.zh: 一个针对稀有异常（占数据的 0.5%）的检测器达到 99.3% 的准确率。解释为什么这个数字可能误导，以及你会改报哪些指标。（2-3 行）

key_points.en: Classes are highly imbalanced: always predicting normal already gives 99.5% accuracy
key_points.zh: 类别高度不平衡：永远预测正常已经有 99.5% 的准确率

key_points.en: So 99.3% may be worse than the trivial baseline and may miss many anomalies
key_points.zh: 所以 99.3% 可能比平凡基线还差，还可能漏掉许多异常

key_points.en: Report recall (share of anomalies caught) and precision (share of alerts that are real), and their trade-off as the threshold moves
key_points.zh: 报告召回率（抓到的异常占比）和精确率（警报里真的占比），以及阈值变化时二者的取舍

model_answer.en: The classes are extremely imbalanced: a trivial detector that always says "normal" already has 99.5% accuracy while catching no anomaly, so 99.3% is no better than doing nothing. Accuracy is dominated by the majority class. I would report recall (the fraction of true anomalies found) together with precision (the fraction of alerts that are real), and show how they trade off as the threshold changes, because raising recall usually increases false positives.
model_answer.zh: The classes are extremely imbalanced: a trivial detector that always says "normal" already has 99.5% accuracy while catching no anomaly, so 99.3% is no better than doing nothing. Accuracy is dominated by the majority class. I would report recall (the fraction of true anomalies found) together with precision (the fraction of alerts that are real), and show how they trade off as the threshold changes, because raising recall usually increases false positives.

explain.en: Name the imbalance, give the baseline number, name the metrics.
explain.zh: 点出不平衡，给出基线的数，说出指标。

title.zh: 为什么要相对密度？（A 部分）

prompt.en: Explain why the distance to the $k$-th nearest neighbour can fail when the data contain regions of different density, and how local outlier factor (LOF) addresses this. (3 lines)
prompt.zh: 解释当数据含有不同密度的区域时，到第 $k$ 个最近邻的距离为什么会失败，以及局部离群因子（LOF）怎样解决。（3 行）

key_points.en: kNN distance is an absolute measure: points in a sparse region have large distances even when normal
key_points.zh: kNN 距离是绝对度量：稀疏区域里的点即使正常距离也大

key_points.en: So an anomaly next to a dense cluster can score lower than normal sparse points; no global threshold works
key_points.zh: 所以紧邻稠密簇的异常得分可能比稀疏区的正常点还低；没有全局阈值行得通

key_points.en: LOF compares a point's local density with the average density of its neighbours; about 1 is normal, much greater than 1 is an outlier
key_points.zh: LOF 把一个点的局部密度和它邻居的平均密度比；约为 1 是正常，远大于 1 是离群

model_answer.en: The distance to the k-th neighbour is an absolute measure: normal points in a sparse region have large distances, so an anomaly beside a dense cluster can get a lower score than normal sparse points, and no single threshold separates them. LOF instead compares the local density of a point with the average density of its k nearest neighbours. A ratio near 1 means the point is as dense as its surroundings (normal); a ratio well above 1 means it is much sparser than its neighbours, so it is an outlier relative to its own neighbourhood.
model_answer.zh: The distance to the k-th neighbour is an absolute measure: normal points in a sparse region have large distances, so an anomaly beside a dense cluster can get a lower score than normal sparse points, and no single threshold separates them. LOF instead compares the local density of a point with the average density of its k nearest neighbours. A ratio near 1 means the point is as dense as its surroundings (normal); a ratio well above 1 means it is much sparser than its neighbours, so it is an outlier relative to its own neighbourhood.

explain.en: The key phrase is *relative to its neighbourhood*.
explain.zh: 关键的一句是*相对它的邻域*。

title.zh: 设计题：检测故障机器（C 部分）

prompt.en: A factory logs 20 sensor readings per second from 500 machines. Fewer than 0.1% of the time a machine is faulty, and these faults are almost never labelled. Design an anomaly detection approach: choose a setting and a method, say how you would score and evaluate it, and name two risks. (A third of a page)
prompt.zh: 一家工厂每秒记录 500 台机器的 20 个传感器读数。机器出故障的时间不到 0.1%，而且这些故障几乎没有标注。设计一个异常检测方案：选择设定和方法，说明怎样打分和评估，并指出两个风险。（约三分之一页）

key_points.en: Setting: unsupervised or semi-supervised (labels of normal operation only); a supervised model is not possible
key_points.zh: 设定：无监督或半监督（只有正常运行的标签）；监督模型不可行

key_points.en: Contextual: normal depends on the machine and its operating mode, so model per machine/mode (contextual attributes) or use relative methods (LOF / cluster-based)
key_points.zh: 上下文：正常取决于机器和运行模式，所以按机器/模式分别建模（上下文属性），或用相对方法（LOF / 基于聚类）

key_points.en: Possibly collective anomalies: look at windows of time rather than single readings
key_points.zh: 可能是集体异常：看时间窗口而不是单个读数

key_points.en: Evaluate with a small labelled sample or injected faults: precision, recall, alert budget; not accuracy
key_points.zh: 用少量标注样本或注入的故障评估：精确率、召回率、警报预算；不用准确率

key_points.en: Risks: false alarms from legitimate new operating modes; concept drift; the contaminated "normal" training data
key_points.zh: 风险：合法的新运行模式引起误报；概念漂移；“正常”训练数据被污染

model_answer.en: Setting: semi-supervised, trained on a period of normal operation, with an unsupervised check. Because normal depends on the machine and its operating mode, I would model each machine and mode separately (the contextual attributes), and score each time window of readings rather than single readings, since a fault often shows as a sequence (a collective anomaly). For the score I would use a local method such as LOF on window features, or a per-mode Gaussian with Mahalanobis distance if the data are roughly Gaussian, with the threshold set by the number of alerts maintenance can handle. Evaluation: with few or no labels, inject known faults or label a small sample and report precision and recall, never accuracy. Risks: false alarms when a legitimate new operating mode appears, and drift over time that makes the "normal" model stale (retrain regularly); also the normal training data may already contain undetected faults.

explain.en: Section C: pick the setting from the labels you have, match the method to the data (context, groups, density), say how you would evaluate with rare labels, and name the risks.
explain.zh: C 部分：由手里的标签选设定，让方法贴合数据（上下文、群、密度），说明标签很少时怎么评估，并点出风险。

items.en: **Anomaly** = generated by a different mechanism; not noise. Types: **point**, **contextual** (contextual vs behavioural attributes), **collective** (needs relations among instances).
items.zh: **异常** = 由另一种机制产生；不是噪声。类型：**点**、**上下文**（上下文属性与行为属性）、**集体**（需要实例间的关系）。

items.en: **Settings:** supervised (both labels, imbalance, accuracy misleading, aim for recall), semi-supervised (normal labels only, false alarms on unseen-but-legitimate), unsupervised (no labels, normal = clustered, false positives).
items.zh: **设定：**监督（两类标签、不平衡、准确率误导、追求召回）、半监督（只有正常标签、对没见过但合法的行为误报）、无监督（没有标签、正常 = 成团、误报）。

items.en: z-score: $z > 3$ is the 99.7% rule, but $z \le \sqrt{N-1}$ always; Mahalanobis uses the covariance, and is for global anomalies; both need a (roughly) Gaussian model.
items.zh: z 分数：$z > 3$ 是 99.7% 规则，但 $z \le \sqrt{N-1}$ 恒成立；马氏距离用协方差，针对全局异常；两者都要（大致）高斯的模型。

items.en: Proximity: distance to the $k$-th neighbour; $O(n^2)$, sensitive to $k$, fails when density varies. Density/LOF: relative to neighbours, $\approx 1$ normal, $\gg 1$ outlier. Clustering: small or distant-from-centre points, size-weighted.
items.zh: 邻近：到第 $k$ 个邻居的距离；$O(n^2)$，对 $k$ 敏感，密度变化时失败。密度/LOF：相对邻居，$\approx 1$ 正常，$\gg 1$ 离群。聚类：小簇或离中心远的点，按簇大小加权。

items.en: Evaluate with **precision and recall**, not accuracy.
items.zh: 评估用**精确率和召回率**，不用准确率。
